newsitem.title: GERMANY: Poll shows most Germans against EMU - paper.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows most Germans against EMU - paper.

text.p: A majority of Germans are against the planned European economic and monetary union (EMU) championed by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, an opinion poll showed on Saturday.

The Infratest Burke financial research institute said only 37 percent of Germans accepted the planned currency union, while 57 percent were against it, the Welt am Sonntag newspaper reported in a release ahead of publication on Sunday.

The poll showed seven out of every 10 citizens thought EMU, due to start in 1999, would happen, although only 40 percent thought Germany would fulfill the conditions laid out in the Maastricht treaty necessary to qualify to take part.

Of those against EMU, most were worried that the planned currency, the euro, would be weaker or less stable than the deutschemark, while others feared that Germany would end up carrying the financial burden of EMU.
The newspaper said 700 citizens with a monthly income of at least 5,000 marks from the states of the former West Germany had taken part in the poll, conducted at the end of last year.
